\section{Weighted sequence spaces}\label{sec:weighted}
\begin{standassump}[Positive weight sequence]\label{ass:weight}
Throughout, $(w_n)_{n\ge 0}$ is a strictly positive sequence with $w_0=1$ and $\sup_n w_{n+1}/w_n < \infty$.
\end{standassump}
\begin{keylem}[Shift boundedness]\label{lem:shift}
The right shift $S$ on $\ell^2_w$ satisfies $\|S\| = \sup_{n\ge 0} (w_{n+1}/w_n)^{1/2}$.
\end{keylem}
\begin{myproof}
For any $x\in\ell^2_w$, $\|Sx\|_w^2 = \sum_{n\ge 0} w_{n+1}|x_n|^2 \le (\sup_n w_{n+1}/w_n)\|x\|_w^2$, and basis vectors saturate the bound.
\end{myproof}
\begin{boxedres}[Weighted contraction fixed point]\label{thm:fixed}
If $T:\ell^2_w\to\ell^2_w$ satisfies $\|Tx-Ty\|_w \le q\|x-y\|_w$ for some $q\in(0,1)$, then $T$ has a unique fixed point $x^*\in\ell^2_w$.
\end{boxedres}
\begin{coro}[Geometric convergence]\label{cor:geom}
The iterates $x_{k+1}=Tx_k$ satisfy $\|x_k - x^*\|_w \le q^k (1-q)^{-1}\|x_1 - x_0\|_w$.
\end{coro}
\begin{obs}
When $w_n = e^{\alpha n}$ with $\alpha>0$, the norm bound equals $e^{\alpha/2}$.
\end{obs}
\begin{cav}
Unbounded ratios $w_{n+1}/w_n$ break the boundedness of the shift operator.
\end{cav}
